title: FAA nationwide ground stop
disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by the FAA, any government agency, airline, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: A nationwide FAA ground stop halted departures at all US airports for more than four hours on Nov 13, 2026. The FAA says operators cancelled about 12,462 flights that day.
who_is_affected: Air travelers on US flights on Nov 13 and the weekend after. By Monday, Nov 16, flights were near normal and the FAA status feed listed no ground stops.

known.text: The FAA ordered a ground stop for all US airports at 3:54 PM ET on Nov 13 (FAA Advisory 111).
The nationwide stop was cancelled at 8:16 PM ET the same day (FAA Advisory 005).
Officials' account: legacy telecom switches and routers were overloaded with data. That is what officials said, not an independent finding.
The FAA's written Q&A names two sites: a radio site in El Dorado, Ark., and a radar site in Amarillo, Texas.
A White House release on Nov 18 says the administration sees no indication of a cyberattack behind the recent outages, the FAA's among them.

not_known.text: The root cause. Investigators recreated the overload in a lab, but no root-cause report is out. The FAA chief said Nov. 19 an announcement was expected that week; none was out by Nov. 22.
Which equipment, site or upgrade set off the overload, and whether the router was faulty or the installation was.
Which specific frequencies or channels went down. None has been named publicly.
Whether a written finding from the FBI, CISA, the DOT Inspector General or the NTSB will follow. None had been published at the last check.

charts.title: How many flights were cancelled?
charts.alt: Cancellations rose from 440 at 5:00 PM to 5,000 at 8:30 PM Eastern on Nov 13.
charts.caption: FlightAware counts via IFR Meter, Fox Weather, ABC7.

charts.title: How many flights were delayed?
charts.alt: Delays stood at 10,000 at 5:30 PM, reached 10,494 at 6:04 PM and were 9,124 at 8:30 PM Eastern on Nov 13.
charts.caption: Same sources; above 10,000 by 5:30 PM.

charts.title: Flights in arrival metering
charts.alt: Flights in arrival metering fell from 646 at 6:03 PM to 136 at 8:23 PM on Nov 13, against about 3,000 at the same times the day before.
charts.caption: Proxy for traffic in the air, per IFR Meter. Blank = no reading.
